description:

infrastructure, to the Roding Valley. The scope of the procurement is to secure professional design services to undertake all necessary design work to advance the projects identified in the Ilford Arrival Spatial Framework and endorsed by Cabinet on 12th September 2024.
The first Contract Award under this procurement was for work from RIBA Stage 0 to RIBA Stage 2. This work was completed in December 2025 and following a Gateway Review it is now appropriate to award a Contract for RIBA Stage 3 that will include the development and submission of a planning application, with professional design support until determination of the application.

title: GB-London: TBG - AI assessment tool
description:
5000 Universal rent verifications are received annually and require manual review and intervention. This requires a full-time post as well as two officers supporting for 6 weeks in the first 2 months of the year
      
      The team send c.600 arrears letters prior to Notie Seeking possession monthly.
      
      UC Verification:
      
      Automation - Enterprise will automate all UC verification processes currently carried out by one full time officer. We receive on average 5000 requests per year with this number increasing yearly due to migration.
      
      Automation is achieved based on a cloud-based solution integrated between the DWPs landlord portal and QL. Enabling to check tenancy details on QL automatically to then provide this information to the DWP without human input.
      
      The above service is currently operated by a number of peers, including The Guiness Partnership, Southern Housing and Redbridge Council as well as others. We have reached out to peers who confirm its success and have seen efficiencies made within the service.
      
      Rent escalation:
      
      This is a new offer from Enterprise based on our discussions with them over the past 12 months.
      
      The income collection service at present manually sends letters based on Mars actions generated. The team currently send on average 600 letter per month, with all members of staff involved in the process.
      
      It is expected the automation of these letters will save 1200 man hours per year, allowing officers to concentrate on early intervention and high arrears activity.
      
      In the first instance the automation will be the 4 stages prior to Notice Seeking possession and will remove all ambiguity and subjectivity.
      
      All vulnerabilities will be excluded for the trial period to ensure a tailored approach can be taken.

title: Newlon Housing Trust - Repairs and Voids Contract
description:
Newlon Housing Trust has completed the procurement of its Repairs and Empty Homes Contract, covering 9,464 units across Camden, Enfield, Hackney, Haringey, Havering, Islington, Newham, Redbridge, Tower Hamlets and Waltham Forest.
The procurement was conducted through a three-stage Competitive Dialogue process in accordance with the Public Contracts Regulations 2015. The contract is let using the JCT Measured Term Contract 2016 (MTC 2016), for an initial period of five years with the option to extend for a further five years.
The contract scope comprises the delivery of responsive repairs (including a 24/7 service) and works to empty homes to bring them to a lettable standard, with the option to include planned works and component replacements at a later stage.
The procurement initially reserved the right to award either to a single provider covering the whole stock or to two providers each covering approximately half. Following evaluation, the contract was awarded as two separate lots:
Lot 1 (4,543 properties) - awarded to Gilmartins
Lot 2 (4,921 properties) - awarded to MNM Property Services Limited
This outcome reflects the agreed approach that one provider may only be awarded a single lot, ensuring that both Gilmartins and MNM were appointed as Newlon's partners for the delivery of these services.

title: 83_25 Supply of Ambient, Chilled, Frozen Foods and Fresh Fruit, Vegetables and Salads
description:
An ESPO multi-supplier framework for the direct supply and delivery of a range of Ambient, Chilled, Frozen Foods and Fresh Fruit, Vegetables and Salad products.

Lot 1 - Ambient, Chilled and Fresh Foods
Lot 2 - Frozen Foods
Lot 3 - Ambient, Chilled, Fresh and Frozen Foods
Lot 4 - Fresh Fruit, Vegetables and Salads

The framework agreement has the option to extend for up to a further 24 months. The total estimated value stated includes the option period.

Food Safety Accreditation - Suppliers must have, and retain throughout the framework lifetime, a relevant third-party food safety accreditation (such as BRC, STS) in relation to the manufacture and/or storage of Food products. Failure to retain such accreditation must be immediately reported to ESPO and will be at the sole discretion of ESPO to suspend or even permanently remove the Supplier from the Framework Agreement. Certificate copies will be sent to ESPO annually, on the expiry/renewal date of such accreditation.

Financial - As part of the on-going contract management process, throughout the period of the Framework Agreement, ESPO shall monitor the financial stability of the awarded Supplier by reference to credit rating agency reports. ESPO shall obtain a credit score for the Supplier on or before the Framework start date as a base score and where a significant change in the credit score is identified over the life of the Framework Agreement, ESPO reserves the right to investigate the reasons for this significant change. Depending on the severity of the changes, it will be at the sole discretion of ESPO to suspend or even permanently remove the Supplier from the Framework Agreement.

title: Boiler Replacement, Old Priory, Leominster
description:
Leominster Town Council wishes to procure an appropriately qualified and accredited plumbing and heating engineer to replace existing plant room boilers, associated ancillary equipment, accompanying pipe work, and controls at the Old Priory site. 

Specifically, this work will include:
-	Isolating gas and electric supplies, taking them back to localised isolation points and testing for soundness.
-	Fully draining the existing heating system.
-	Removal of all redundant equipment, boilers, flues, pipework, pumps etc.
-	Installation of 2 x 70kw gas condensing boilers, with flues and air ducts according to the manufacturer's specifications.
-	Provision of new pumped primary boiler circuit (from boiler shunt pumps to the plate heat exchanger)
-	Provision of new secondary distribution circuits within the plant room.
-	Provision of one new automatic system pressurization unit (one to be retained)
-	Installation of new BMS controls for the boilers and heating system, including zoning and thermostatic time controls.
-	Installation of new electrical control panel.
-	Flushing and recharging the heating system, including corrosion inhibitor.
-	Commissioning of new boilers and instructing staff on use of controls.
-	2 years of servicing and system support
-	5 year minimum guarantee (to cover boiler hardware and software) The
-	boilers MUST be commissioned by the manufacturer to obtain this warranty.
 
Works must:
-	Include appropriate lighting, signing and guarding to protect members of the public for the duration of the works.
-	Include issuing of all industry standard certificates for the works
-	Comply with all Scheduled Monument Consent requirements communicated by the client
-	Leave the site clean, tidy and ready for use.

Tenderers are:
-	required to inspect and examine the site and its surroundings before submitting their tenders 
-	advised to obtain all necessary information which they feel is necessary to submit their tender.

It will be a condition of the invitation to tender that the tenderer should not at any time prior to notification of the award of the contract disclose to or otherwise discuss with any other tenderer or any other third party its actual or intended tender price or any approximation of that price. Your indication that you wish to submit a tender will be taken as acceptance of that condition. The client offers no guarantee that the lowest or any tender will be recommended for acceptance or accepted. The client will not be responsible for any cost incurred in the preparation of any tender. 

All tenderers are to complete sections 4-12 of the supplied RFT form, along with a tender summary spreadsheet, and return their submission by Sunday 15th December 2024 at midnight to: boilerprocurement@leominstertowncouncil.gov.uk  

Contract queries must be submitted by email to Liz Womack at e.womack@leominstertowncouncil.gov.uk in advance of 5pm Monday 9th December 2024.
